fixes.title: Turn Microsoft Defender back on
fixes.why: Without antivirus, ransomware can run unnoticed.
steps: Click Start and open Windows Security.
Choose Virus & threat protection, then Manage settings.
If it switches itself off again, ask your IT helper to check for other security software.

fixes.title: Update or remove outdated programs
fixes.why: Old versions of everyday programs have known holes that attackers use.
steps: Look for Help, then About or Check for updates, and install the update.

fixes.title: Start backing up your files with File History
fixes.why: If ransomware locks your files, a recent backup is the only way to get them back for free.
steps: Plug in an external USB drive with enough space for your files.
Click Start, type File History and open it.
Choose the USB drive and click Turn on.
Click Run now to make the first backup.
Unplug the drive when it finishes and store it away from the PC.

fixes.title: Install the latest Windows updates
fixes.why: Missing updates are the most common way attackers get into a PC.
steps: Save your work and close your programs.
Click Start, open Settings and go to Windows Update.
Click Check for updates, then Download and install.

fixes.title: Plan your move to a supported Windows version
fixes.why: Old Windows versions stop getting security fixes, so new attacks stay open.
steps: Click Start, open Settings and go to Windows Update.
If an upgrade to Windows 11 is offered, back up your files first, then install it.
If this PC can't run Windows 11, ask your IT helper about Extended Security Updates or a new PC.
